Usage: headroom headless [<command>] [flags]
   or: headroom headless [flags]

Place sessions a headless runner starts itself, on per-account tokens.

For a caller that runs Claude Code sessions headless under a config dir of its own — an
eval runner — and wants them spread over the subscriptions the way automatic launches
spread. headroom decides and records; the caller starts the session itself, on the
account's headless token. The caller's contract is docs/specs/headless.md.

Bare, it lists every account's headless token: whether there is one, when it ends, and why
a placement would not choose the account. Tokens are never shown here.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help       Show context-sensitive help.
      --version    Print the build this binary is — its commit and the commit's time — and exit.

Arguments and flags of list, the default command:
      --json       Print the listing as JSON.

Commands:
  list                         List every account's headless token: whether there is one, and when
                               it ends (default).
  mint <account>               Mint a long-lived token for one account through claude setup-token.
  place                        Decide which account the next headless session spends, and record it.
  started <placement> <pid>    Report the process a session placed by place runs as, so it counts
                               while it runs.
  token <account>              Print one account's headless token, and nothing else.
  forget <account>             Forget one account's headless token.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed
  2    invalid arguments, nothing was run; for check, an assertion it could not test (INCONCLUSIVE)
  3    headless place refused: every account it could take is near a limit or excluded; login start,
       finish or cancel refused, nothing spent or sent: the document's reason says why

Run "headroom headless <command> --help" for a command's details.
